beats.text: A Dorset farmer did it in 1774.
beats.note: When smallpox reached Yetminster, Benjamin Jesty took his wife and two sons to a cow with cowpox and scratched the material into their arms with a darning needle.
Jesty and two female servants had caught it. Wikipedia cites the folk belief that dairy workers were protected from smallpox.
Wikipedia says he was hooted at, reviled and pelted at markets. Some feared people would turn into horned beasts.

beats.context: Wikipedia counts that gap between Jesty's family and Jenner's experiment in 1796.

beats.note: He inoculated eight year old James Phipps with cowpox from a dairymaid, Sarah Nelmes, according to Morabia. Nature says it is not clear whether Jenner knew of earlier cases like Jesty's.
That was in June 1802, with 20,000 pounds more in 1807. Jesty received a testimonial and a pair of gold mounted lancets.

beats.text: First is not the same as famous.
